dedupe_keys.name: tamera water retention landscape against drought and desertification alentejo

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the Water Retention Landscape built on the 154-hectare Tamera farm and eco-village in Alentejo, the most arid region of Portugal, to counter erosion, desertification and drought. A water retention landscape keeps rain where it falls: Tamera combined lakes and ponds with clay-sealed dams, reforestation and mixed ground cover, holistic grazing, keyline design, terraces, swales and infiltration of road and roof runoff. Design and construction ran from 2006 to 2015, followed by smaller works and maintenance. Since 2011 the community has met all its drinking water needs from wells fed by the landscape, and a new spring appeared after the first lake was built. A cost-benefit analysis used net present value over 2015-2050 at a 3 percent discount rate; quantified benefits include transitional woodland growing from 9.34 to 19.50 hectares and about 810,000 euros of net income from tourism and water events. The page, first published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with links to the Tamera site. Caveats: investment can be around half a million euros, several benefits could not be quantified and the legal framework was complex. It illustrates nature-based drought and water-scarcity hazard reduction and climate adaptation at farm scale; related records are the Altovicentino natural water retention measures and Serchio nature-based solutions case studies.
name: Tamera water retention landscape against drought and desertification (Alentejo)
outcomes: The landscape has supplied all of Tamera's drinking water from wells since 2011, doubled transitional woodland and created a new year-round spring.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the Tamera initiative
